R07.reason: A custom error handler's body is unknown to Zinc, so the 500 is documented without one.
findings: GET /boom: sent a text/plain body for 500, documented none

R14.reason: Automatic HEAD is answered by Zinc but isn't an operation in the spec.
findings: HEAD /v: no matching operation in the spec

R15.reason: Automatic OPTIONS isn't an operation in the spec.
findings: OPTIONS /v: no matching operation in the spec

R16.reason: A 405 for an unregistered method isn't per operation.
findings: DELETE /v: no matching operation in the spec

R19.reason: A status error the route doesn't declare with Errors can't be known to the spec.

R23.reason: Without the recover middleware, a panic reaches net/http, as documented.
findings: GET /panic: the handler's panic reached net/http: boom

R30.reason: The handler writes a body its output type doesn't describe; no spec can know. Return zinc.Bytes with Produces (R21).

S08.reason: An unknown security scheme name is an error, by design.
findings: OpenAPISpec: zinc: GET /x names security scheme "nope", which OpenAPIConfig.SecuritySchemes doesn't define

V05.reason: Registering the spec route on a path already in use panics, like any duplicate route.
findings: building the app panicked: route already registered for /openapi.json

X16.reason: Two runtime routes that OpenAPI sees as one operation are an error when the spec is built (F02).
findings: OpenAPISpec: zinc: routes GET /files/{path} and GET /files/{path...} are the same OpenAPI operation, GET /files/{path}; hide one with Route.Hidden

X17.reason: Paths that differ only in parameter names are an error when the spec is built, as OpenAPI forbids them (F02).
findings: OpenAPISpec: zinc: paths /pets/{id} and /pets/{name} differ only in parameter names, which OpenAPI doesn't allow; give the parameters the same names
